reasoning.Student A:
My goal is to maximize my chances of getting into my most preferred school. I should stick to my true preferences because the algorithm protects me from being "knocked out" of a school that would have accepted me. Rejections only redirect me to schools I ranked lower.

Therefore, I will rank the schools in the order of my true preferences: z > x > w > y. My priority rank at each school does not change this, as my preference order determines the order in which I'm considered. Even if many applicants favor y > x > w > z, that doesn't change my preferences or the algorithm's guarantee that rejections only redirect and never eliminate.
